title: Interpolate with extrapolation
summary: Piecewise linear interpolation with extend, clamp and identity modes.
prompt: Write `interpolate(value, { inputRange, outputRange, extrapolate, extrapolateLeft, extrapolateRight })`. Ranges have the same length (at least 2) and `inputRange` must be non-decreasing; otherwise throw an error mentioning `inputRange`. Find the segment containing `value` and map it linearly. Outside the range, apply the mode for that side (`extrapolateLeft`/`extrapolateRight`, falling back to `extrapolate`, default `'extend'`): `extend` continues the nearest end segment, `clamp` returns the end output, `identity` returns `value` unchanged. If a segment has zero input width, return its start output. There is no React Native runtime here, so this is modelled as plain TypeScript.
hints: Pick the segment `i` where `value <= inputRange[i + 1]`, or the last one.
